Intl Applicants via Common App
2025-26 Cycle YoY

keyDates.text: OBBBA student loan changes take effect: Grad PLUS loans eliminated for new borrowers; annual graduate loan cap set at $20,500 ($100K lifetime) and professional at $50,000 ($200K lifetime). Court stay on ED's narrow 'professional degree' definition creates compliance uncertainty.

Court-ordered joint status report due from parties in nurse practitioner/PA loan limits lawsuit (American Association of Nurse Practitioners v. McMahon), with proposed schedule for further proceedings.

New tiered endowment excise tax takes effect under OBBBA for private universities with >3,000 tuition-paying students. Top rate: 8% for institutions with >$2M endowment per student (Harvard, Yale, MIT, Stanford).

OBBBA repayment reform: New borrowers on or after July 1 may only enroll in tiered Standard or Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP). Legacy income-driven plans (SAVE, PAYE, ICR) sunset for all borrowers by July 1, 2028.

Fall 2026 semester begins for most Ivy League and peer institutions. First full enrollment cycle under OBBBA borrowing caps and new endowment tax regime. Financial aid offices monitoring enrollment impacts.

Early Decision I and Early Action deadlines for Class of 2031 at most selective institutions. First cycle fully under OBBBA era; Brown, Cornell, Dartmouth, Penn, and Yale have reinstated test requirements.

First Circuit Court of Appeals expected to hear Trump administration's appeal seeking reinstatement of ~$2.7B Harvard funding freeze, challenging Judge Burroughs's September 2025 ruling that cuts were unlawful.

Yale-DOJ settlement status remains unresolved. Yale has submitted a formal proposal to avoid a Columbia-style agreement; outcome will set a precedent for undergraduate and law school admissions oversight nationwide.
